insights.label: Activity is real, but definitions differ
insights.summary: Knight Frank-reported H1 sales rose 5% year-on-year to 27,968 units, while JLL separately reports approximately 17,000 units of Q2 demand. These are market-research measures, not registrations, so they show activity rather than legal transfers.

insights.label: Inventory pressure is the clearest risk signal
insights.summary: Unsold inventory rose 22% year-on-year to 74,299 units and the city-wide time-to-sell was 5.3 quarters. That means buyers should inspect project-level inventory and absorption rather than assume city-wide demand means every project is moving.

insights.label: South looks more inventory-heavy than East or North
insights.summary: South Bengaluru had 33,534 unsold units and 7.4 quarters to sell, versus East at 4.9 and North at 3.9. This is a corridor-level screening signal, not a verdict on an individual project.

insights.label: New supply is substantial and concentrated
insights.summary: Knight Frank-reported H1 launches were 34,749 units, while Cushman reported H1 launches crossing 25,000. The gap is a methodology warning; both sources still indicate substantial supply. South, East and North account for most launches.

method: Insights are derived from independently published observations. Figures are not combined when definitions or periods are not like-for-like. No registration count is inferred.

trend.label: Current trend: active, but cooling at the margin
trend.answer: Bengaluru is not showing a simple boom or collapse. The latest same-source comparison shows Q2 2026 sales up 47% year-on-year and launches up 71% year-on-year, which means activity is expanding. But JLL reports Q2 demand down 6% quarter-on-quarter, while supply is growing faster than sales in the PropEquity comparison. The practical reading is: demand is still strong, but buyers may have more choice and negotiating leverage than the headline sales number suggests.
signals: Knight Frank: H1 2026 sales +5% YoY and launches +4% YoY
Knight Frank: unsold inventory +22% YoY; 5.3 quarters to sell
trend.method: Trend direction prioritises same-publisher period comparisons. Cross-publisher figures are used as corroboration, not added together.
